title: Unify Python SDK streaming chat event model and ergonomic handlers
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: The Python SDK currently exposes multiple ad-hoc streaming APIs for chat completions: low-level raw byte streams, callback-style hooks, and an async iterator helper. Consumers are confused about which pattern to pick for error handling, retries, and backpressure. Several internal customers have implemented fragile glue code to convert between styles (callbacks -> async iterators) and to resume interrupted streams.

Goal: Provide a single, ergonomic event-first streaming API surface for chat completions that: 1) exposes a typed event model (message.delta, message.finish, error, meta, heartbeat), 2) supports easy consumption via async iteration, callbacks, and a sync convenience wrapper for fast prototyping, 3) defines clear retry/resume semantics for idempotent requests, and 4) gives guidance and primitives for consumer backpressure and cancellation.

Scope: Design the event enum and Python classes, implement the public API in the next minor release, add comprehensive examples (callback, async for, sync iterator), add tests for resume/retry behavior with simulated flaky network and server side reconnects, and update docs and migration guide. Not in scope: changing underlying server streaming protocol or other language SDKs (we will design the model to be portable).

Acceptance criteria: 
- New Python API exposes a StreamingChatClient with a .stream_completion(request) method that returns a StreamingEvent async iterator.
- The StreamingEvent model contains well-documented types: START, TOKEN, DELTA, END, ERROR, HEARTBEAT, METADATA.
- Consumers can pass an on_event callback to .stream_completion and can also use async for event in stream.
- Retry policy utilities exist (idempotency keys, resumable token offsets) and tests verify a streamed response can be resumed once after transient connection failures without duplicate tokens when using idempotent requests.
- Backpressure guidance and an example using a bounded asyncio.Queue are included in the examples folder.
- Documentation and migration guide created in docs/sdk/python/streaming.md with code samples and tradeoffs.

Design decisions summary: 
- Use an explicit Event dataclass with a small enum string tag rather than ad-hoc dicts to make type hints useful and to avoid subtle key mismatches.
- Expose both callback and async iterator to avoid forcing users into a single pattern; implement callbacks as a thin wrapper around the iterator to keep a single canonical code path.
- Implement resumable streams via server-provided token offsets when available; fall back to conservative retry that replays last N tokens when offset is missing.
- Leave sync wrapper as convenience for notebook flows; recommend async for production to avoid hidden threading issues.

Open questions: 
- Should the SDK surface an explicit ACK mechanism for downstream processing (likely no for now)?
- How to best encode partial-edits when a model sends revision deltas vs token deltas? (we propose a DELTA subtype with subkind field).

Risks: 
- Increased surface area and API churn for existing users; include a clear migration guide and deprecation schedule.
- Complex resume semantics across multiple model variants; implement conservative default and allow opt-in aggressive modes.
